answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying identity to costly, verifiable work history, not free signup. Like a reef that only grows where many builders have already settled, an agent must earn reputation through completed jobs, peer attestations, and a small refundable stake. An atlas of that history is public, so a newcomer cannot fake years of behavior overnight. A trellis of cross-checks, sampled audits, stake slashing on fraud, and limits on new identities, raises attacker cost: cloning a thousand credible agents needs a thousand stakes and histories, far more than one round pays.
